name: Civic Education
topics: Values: honesty, integrity, contentment, discipline and cooperation
Constitutional democracy and the pillars of democracy
Drug abuse, cultism and youth empowerment
Nigerian national symbols and federal institutions

questions.q: Which of the following statements best defines honesty as a civic value?
o: Being satisfied with one's present condition in life
Strictly obeying all school rules without question
Working together with others to achieve a common goal
Being truthful and free from fraud or deception in one's dealings
questions.e: Honesty means being truthful, sincere, and free from deceit or fraud when dealing with people. It is about saying and doing what is true and right.
questions.p: Honesty na to dey tell true and no gree cheat person for any dealing wey you get with am. Na truth and sincerity dem dey talk about here.

questions.q: Which of these best describes discipline as a value?
o: Being content with little resources
Training oneself to obey rules and control one's conduct
Refusing to accept bribe from anybody
Sharing your resources with people around you
questions.e: Discipline is the act of training oneself to follow rules, control one's behaviour, and act in an orderly manner at all times. The other options describe cooperation, contentment and honesty respectively.
questions.p: Discipline na when person train imself make e dey follow rule and control imself well well. The other options na for cooperation, contentment and honesty.

questions.q: Tunde is the treasurer of his class association. Although he has access to the association's funds, he keeps accurate records, refuses to divert any money for personal use, and conducts himself the same way whether people are watching him or not. Tunde's behaviour best illustrates which value?
o: Cooperation
Contentment
Integrity
Discipline
questions.e: Integrity means remaining consistently honest and upright in character, even when no one is supervising. Tunde's unwavering good conduct with the funds, with or without supervision, shows integrity.
questions.p: Integrity na when person still dey do correct correct thing even as nobody dey watch am. Na so Tunde take manage the class money well.

questions.q: Mrs. Bello earns a modest salary as a primary school teacher. Instead of complaining or envying her wealthier neighbours, she manages her income wisely and expresses gratitude for what she has. This attitude best demonstrates which value?
o: Contentment
Honesty
Cooperation
Discipline
questions.e: Contentment means being satisfied with what one has instead of being envious of other people's possessions. Mrs. Bello's gratitude and acceptance of her situation clearly show contentment.
questions.p: Contentment na when person satisfy with wetin e get, no dey envy another person property. Na so Mrs Bello dey manage im life.

questions.q: During a community sanitation exercise in Ikorodu, residents from different streets combined their efforts, shared tools, and worked together to clear the drainage channels before the rainy season. This action best demonstrates which value?
o: Discipline
Cooperation
Contentment
Integrity
questions.e: Cooperation means working together with others towards achieving a common goal. The residents combining their efforts and tools to clear the drainages is a clear example of cooperation.
questions.p: Cooperation na when people come together to work as one for better result. Na so the Ikorodu people take clean their gutters together.

questions.q: Mr. Okafor supervises a road construction project. He personally checks the quality of materials used daily, reports any substandard work to his superiors, and ensures the job meets the required standard even while his supervisor is away on leave and cannot monitor him. Which combination of values is Mr. Okafor MOST demonstrating?
o: Contentment and cooperation
Discipline and contentment
Integrity and discipline
Honesty and cooperation
questions.e: Mr. Okafor shows discipline by maintaining standards without being supervised, and integrity by doing what is right consistently even when no one is watching. Both values together best explain his conduct.
questions.p: Mr Okafor dey show discipline because e dey follow standard even without supervisor, and integrity because e dey do correct thing anytime anytime. Na these two values explain am well.

questions.q: A group of market women agreed to contribute money weekly into a cooperative society to support members financially. However, one member, Iya Kemi, consistently refuses to pay her contribution but still expects support whenever she is in need. Which value is Iya Kemi LACKING that is most central to the success of the cooperative society?
o: Contentment
Honesty
Discipline
Cooperation
questions.e: Cooperation requires every member of a group to play their own part for the common good. Iya Kemi's refusal to contribute while still expecting benefits shows a lack of cooperation, which threatens the survival of the society.
questions.p: Cooperation mean say everybody must do their own part make the group work well. Iya Kemi no dey contribute money but e wan chop benefit, so e no get cooperation.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'national consciousness' as used in Civic Education?
o: Awareness and pride in belonging to one's country
Loyalty to one's ethnic group above the nation
Preference for one's state over others
Knowledge of the local government by-laws
questions.e: National consciousness means being aware of, and proud of, belonging to one's country as a whole, not just to a smaller group. It makes citizens see themselves first as Nigerians.
questions.p: National consciousness na say you know and dey proud say you be citizen of your country, no be just your tribe or state. E make person see imself as Nigerian first.

questions.q: The National Pledge, which Nigerian pupils recite in schools, is mainly meant to express the reciter's:
o: Commitment to loyalty and service to Nigeria
Support for a particular political party
Obedience to the school head teacher
Respect for traditional rulers only
questions.e: The National Pledge is a promise of loyalty, faithfulness and service to Nigeria as a united nation. It is not tied to any school authority, traditional ruler or political party.
questions.p: National Pledge na promise wey show say you go loyal, faithful and ready to serve Nigeria well well. E no be about school head teacher, king or any political party.

questions.q: Which of these attitudes poses the greatest threat to national unity in a multi-ethnic country like Nigeria?
o: Inter-ethnic marriage between citizens
Use of a common official language in government offices
Ethnic bigotry and tribalism in public appointments
Celebration of national festivals by all groups
questions.e: Ethnic bigotry and tribalism create division because people are favoured or rejected based on tribe instead of merit. This weakens trust and cooperation among Nigerians from different groups.
questions.p: Ethnic bigotry and tribalism dey cause division because dem dey favour or reject people because of tribe instead of merit. Dis one dey spoil trust and cooperation among Nigerians.

questions.q: Which of the following is correctly described as a symbol of Nigeria's national identity?
o: The logo of a local government council
The green-white-green national flag
The coat of arms of Lagos State
The badge of a private secondary school
questions.e: The green-white-green flag represents the whole of Nigeria and is recognised internationally as a national symbol. State and local symbols only represent smaller parts of the country.
questions.p: Di green-white-green flag na symbol wey represent di whole Nigeria, and di world sabi am well well. State or local government symbols na just for small part of di country.

questions.q: The federal character principle, as applied in Nigeria's public service appointments, is mainly designed to:
o: Allow only the most populated states to control key offices
Make sure every state gets equal share of oil revenue
Give preference to candidates from the ruling party
Ensure fair representation of the different states and ethnic groups in government positions
questions.e: Federal character is a constitutional principle that ensures no single ethnic group, state or section dominates public appointments, so that all parts of Nigeria feel included. It is about representation, not revenue sharing or party politics.
questions.p: Federal character na constitutional rule wey make sure say no single tribe, state or area dey control public appointment alone, so dat everybody for Nigeria go feel say dem dey part of am. E no be about sharing oil money or party politics.

questions.q: During postings, some officials of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) decide to always post corps members to serve only in their own states of origin, instead of mixing them across different states. This practice would mainly defeat the scheme's original aim of:
o: Promoting national integration among young Nigerians
Teaching corps members a new trade
Supplying free labour to rural communities
Reducing graduate unemployment
questions.e: NYSC was set up so graduates can live and work outside their home areas, mix with other cultures, and build friendships across Nigeria. Posting people only to their own states removes this cross-cultural exposure and weakens national integration.
questions.p: Dem start NYSC make graduates fit live and work outside dia own area so dem go mix wit other culture and make friend across Nigeria. If dem only post pesin go im own state, e go spoil dis cross-cultural mixing wey dey build national integration.

questions.q: A community leader in a Nigerian town encourages young people to marry across ethnic lines, insists that government offices attend to everyone in a common language, and ensures job opportunities are not based on tribe. These actions by the leader are best described as efforts to promote:
o: State autonomy
Local government reform
Political party loyalty
National integration
questions.e: Encouraging inter-ethnic marriage, a common language and tribe-free opportunities are all ways of bringing different groups together as one people, which is exactly what national integration means. None of the actions relate to party loyalty, state autonomy or local government structure.
questions.p: To support marriage across tribe, common language for office, and job wey no depend on tribe, na way to bring different people togeda as one, and dat na wetin national integration mean. Di actions no concern party loyalty, state autonomy or local government matter.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines the term 'citizenship' as used in Civic Education?
o: The act of living in a foreign country for many years
The legal status of belonging to a particular nation, with rights and obligations attached
The ability to speak the official language of a country fluently
The possession of a national identity card
questions.e: Citizenship is a legal relationship between a person and a state, which comes with rights (like voting) and duties (like obeying laws). Speaking a language or holding an ID card does not by itself make someone a citizen.
questions.p: Citizenship na legal connection between person and him country, and e carry rights and duties. To sabi talk language or get ID card no mean say you be citizen.

questions.q: Which of these is a civic duty expected of every Nigerian citizen?
o: Criticising government officials publicly
Demanding salary increase from government
Obeying the laws of the land
Travelling abroad for holidays
questions.e: Obeying the laws of the land is a basic civic duty that keeps order in society and allows government to function well. The other options are personal choices or rights, not duties.
questions.p: To obey law na duty wey every citizen suppose do so that society go dey orderly. The other options na personal choice or right, no be duty.

questions.q: Chidi, a 20-year-old undergraduate, was arrested by the police and kept in detention for three weeks without being charged to court. Which of his fundamental rights was violated?
o: Right to freedom of expression
Right to own property
Right to freedom of movement
Right to personal liberty
questions.e: The right to personal liberty protects a person from being detained beyond the legal time limit without trial. Nigerian law requires that a suspect be charged to court within a reasonable time, usually within 48 hours except in special cases.
questions.p: Right to personal liberty na the one wey protect person from dey lock up pass the time wey law allow without court case. Law talk say dem suppose charge person go court fast fast, no be three weeks.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa, a citizen of Niger Republic, wishes to become a naturalized citizen of Nigeria. Which of the following is NOT one of the requirements he must satisfy under Nigerian law?
o: He must renounce his original citizenship immediately after birth
He must be of good character
He must have resided in Nigeria continuously for a minimum period of time
He must show that he can contribute meaningfully to Nigeria's development
questions.e: Naturalization applies to adults seeking citizenship, so 'renouncing citizenship immediately after birth' makes no logical sense and is not a real requirement. Genuine requirements include residency period, good character, and ability to contribute to national growth.
questions.p: Naturalization na for grown-up wey wan become citizen, so 'to renounce citizenship immediately after birth' no make sense at all and e no be real requirement. The real ones be say you must don stay long time, get good character, and fit contribute to the country.

questions.q: Which of the following rights is classified as a socio-economic right rather than a civil right under the Nigerian Constitution?
o: Right to fair hearing
Right to education
Right to private life
Right to freedom of thought
questions.e: The right to education falls under the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy, which deal with socio-economic goals. Fair hearing, freedom of thought and private life are civil rights found in the fundamental human rights chapter.
questions.p: Right to education dey under the part of constitution wey talk about socio-economic goals. Fair hearing, freedom of thought and private life na civil rights wey dey the fundamental human rights chapter.

questions.q: During a community town hall meeting, the chairman reminded the people that paying taxes, defending the nation when called upon, and respecting constituted authority are things they owe to the state. These are best described as:
o: Political rights
Economic rights
Civic duties and obligations
Fundamental human rights
questions.e: Paying tax, defending the nation, and respecting authority are obligations citizens owe the state in return for the protection and services they enjoy, so they are civic duties, not rights. Rights are benefits citizens receive, while duties are responsibilities they must perform.
questions.p: To pay tax, defend the country, and respect authority na things citizen owe the government, so na duty, no be right. Right na wetin citizen dey enjoy, duty na wetin dem suppose do.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines human rights?
o: Basic entitlements that belong to every person simply because they are human
Privileges given by government only to loyal citizens
Benefits that are reserved only for working-class citizens
Special rewards given to citizens who obey all laws
questions.e: Human rights are natural entitlements that every person has simply by being human, not favours granted by government. They are universal and not tied to employment or obedience to law.
questions.p: Human rights na basic things wey every human being get just because dem be human, e no be favour wey government dey give to only people wey dem like. Na everybody get am, no condition dey attach to am.

questions.q: In the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as amended), the Fundamental Human Rights of citizens are contained in which Chapter?
o: Chapter III
Chapter IV
Chapter I
Chapter II
questions.e: Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution (Sections 33 to 46) specifically lists and protects the Fundamental Human Rights of every Nigerian, such as the right to life, dignity and fair hearing.
questions.p: Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution na im get all the Fundamental Human Rights, from Section 33 to 46, like right to life, dignity and fair hearing.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a civil right, as opposed to a political right?
o: The right to vote during an election
The right to register and belong to a political party
The right to contest for a public office
The right to a fair hearing before a court of law
questions.e: Civil rights protect a person's basic freedom and justice, such as the right to fair hearing. Voting, contesting elections and joining political parties are political rights that concern participation in government.
questions.p: Civil right na im dey protect person freedom and justice, like right to fair hearing. But voting, contesting election and joining political party na political rights wey dey concern how person take take part for government.

questions.q: Which Nigerian government agency was specifically established to combat the trafficking of persons, especially women and children, for forced labour and prostitution?
o: National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)
Independent Corrupt Practices Commission (ICPC)
National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP)
Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
questions.e: NAPTIP was set up by law in Nigeria mainly to investigate and prosecute cases of human trafficking and to support victims. EFCC deals with financial crimes, ICPC with corruption, and NDLEA with illegal drugs.
questions.p: NAPTIP na the agency wey Nigeria government set up to fight human trafficking, especially for women and children. EFCC na for financial crime, ICPC na for corruption, NDLEA na for drug matter.

questions.q: During a state of emergency declared because of violent clashes in a town, the government imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew that restricted people from moving about at night. Which right is being legally limited by this action?
o: Freedom of movement
Right to dignity of the human person
Freedom from torture
Right to life
questions.e: A curfew directly restricts people's freedom of movement, which the law allows the government to limit temporarily for public safety during an emergency. Rights like the right to life and freedom from torture cannot be taken away even in emergencies.
questions.p: Curfew na im dey restrict people movement, and law allow government to limit dis kind right small-small when emergency happen for public safety. But rights like right to life and freedom from torture no fit cancel even for emergency.

questions.q: Mr. Udoh was arrested by the police and kept in detention for five days without being told the reason for his arrest or taken to court. Which of his fundamental rights has been violated?
o: Right to private and family life
Right to freedom of association
Right to personal liberty
Right to freedom of thought and religion
questions.e: The right to personal liberty requires that a person be told the reason for arrest promptly and be brought to court within a reasonable time. Keeping Mr. Udoh for five days without charge or explanation breaches this right.
questions.p: Right to personal liberty mean say dem must tell person why dem arrest am sharp-sharp and carry am go court within reasonable time. Since dem keep Mr. Udoh for five days without tell am anything or carry am go court, na im personal liberty dem violate.

questions.q: A government shut down a private radio station after it broadcast a message that incited ethnic violence in a community. This action by the government is best described as an example of what?
o: Derogation of rights that only applies during war time
Complete abolition of fundamental rights in the country
Total enjoyment of absolute rights by all citizens
Limitation of rights in the interest of public order
questions.e: Freedom of expression is not absolute; the law allows it to be limited where its exercise threatens public order, safety or the rights of others. This is a lawful limitation, not a total removal or war-time derogation of rights.
questions.p: Freedom of expression no be absolute right; law fit limit am if e go cause wahala for public order or safety. Na lawful limitation be dis, e no mean say dem don cancel the right completely or say na only for war time e dey apply.

questions.q: In Civic Education, the term 'rule of law' basically means that:
o: only the police have power to interpret and enforce the law
the law is supreme and binds everyone, including government officials
traditional rulers have final say in all legal matters
the President can make laws without the National Assembly
questions.e: Rule of law means no one, not even government officials, is above the law. Everyone, from the ordinary citizen to the highest office holder, must obey the law and can be held accountable under it.
questions.p: Rule of law mean say law dey reign supreme for everybody, even government people. Nobody dey above the law, from ordinary person to oga at the top.

questions.q: Which principle of the rule of law states that a person should only be punished for an offence after it has been clearly proved in a competent court of law?
o: Fiscal federalism
Due process of law
Supremacy of the constitution
Separation of powers
questions.e: Due process of law requires that before anyone is punished, they must be given a fair hearing and the offence must be proved in court. This protects citizens from arbitrary punishment.
questions.p: Due process of law mean say dem must first prove say person do wetin dem accuse am for court before dem fit punish am. E dey protect person from wahala wey no follow law.

questions.q: The concept of the rule of law, with its three classical principles, is most closely associated with which British jurist?
o: John Locke
Jean-Jacques Rousseau
A.V. Dicey
Baron de Montesquieu
questions.e: A.V. Dicey, a British constitutional lawyer, popularised the modern concept of rule of law in the 19th century, outlining supremacy of law, equality before the law, and the role of ordinary courts in protecting rights.
questions.p: Na A.V. Dicey, one British law man, popularise rule of law for 19th century. E talk about law wey dey supreme, equality before law, and ordinary court wey dey protect people right.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised feature of the rule of law?
o: Arbitrary arrest and detention of citizens without trial
Supremacy of the law over individuals and government
Independence of the judiciary from government control
Equality of all persons before the law
questions.e: Arbitrary arrest and detention without trial is exactly what the rule of law opposes, since it denies people a fair hearing. The other options are true features that protect citizens and limit government power.
questions.p: Arbitrary arrest without trial na the opposite of rule of law, because e dey deny person fair hearing. The other options na correct features wey dey protect citizens.

questions.q: A state governor orders soldiers to demolish a trader's shop in Onitsha market without any court order, notice or hearing given to the trader. This action directly violates which principle of the rule of law?
o: Separation of powers
Fiscal responsibility
Federal character principle
Due process of law
questions.e: Due process requires that a person be given fair hearing and proper legal procedure before action is taken against their property or rights. Demolishing the shop without court order or notice breaches this principle.
questions.p: Due process say make dem give person fair hearing and follow correct legal process before dem touch im property. To demolish the shop without court order na breach of this principle.

questions.q: Two drivers in Kaduna are caught driving against traffic on the same day. One is an ordinary commercial driver who is arrested and prosecuted, while the other, a serving senator, is quietly released by the police without any charge. This scenario shows a clear violation of which principle of the rule of law?
o: Supremacy of the constitution
Independence of the judiciary
Equality before the law
Due process of law
questions.e: Equality before the law means all persons, regardless of status, should face the same legal treatment for the same offence. Releasing the senator while prosecuting the ordinary driver shows unequal treatment, which breaches this principle.
questions.p: Equality before law mean say everybody, no matter who you be, suppose face the same legal treatment for same offence. To release senator but prosecute ordinary driver na clear unequal treatment.

questions.q: Which of these situations best shows the rule of law working properly in a society?
o: A soldier assaults a civilian but is tried under special military protection, away from regular courts
A government minister seizes a private company's property by executive order without any compensation
A police officer keeps a suspect in detention for two weeks without taking him to court
A traditional chief accused of fraud is tried in a regular Magistrate court like any other citizen, with a right to appeal
questions.e: The rule of law demands that everyone, including highly placed persons, be subject to the same courts and legal procedures as ordinary citizens. Trying the chief in a regular court with a right to appeal shows equality before the law and due process in action.
questions.p: Rule of law want say everybody, even big men, go face the same court and legal process like ordinary person. To try the chief for regular court with right to appeal na correct example of equality before law and due process.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines democracy?
o: Government of the people, by the people and for the people
Government by the military council
Government controlled by one political party
Government based on hereditary succession to the throne
questions.e: Democracy is a system where the people choose their leaders and the leaders rule with the consent of the people. This classic definition shows that power belongs to the citizens.
questions.p: Democracy na system wey di pipo dem get power to choose dia leaders, and di leaders dey rule with di pipo consent. Na dis definition show say power na for di citizens.

questions.q: Which body is constitutionally responsible for organising and conducting elections into federal and state offices in Nigeria?
o: Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)
Independent Corrupt Practices Commission (ICPC)
questions.e: INEC is the independent body set up to register voters, conduct elections and announce results in Nigeria. The other agencies deal with crime, drugs and corruption, not elections.
questions.p: INEC na di body wey dey register voters, conduct election and announce result for Nigeria. Di oda agencies dey handle crime, drug and corruption matter, no be election.

questions.q: According to the Nigerian constitution, what is the minimum voting age for a citizen to be registered and vote in elections?
o: 16 years
18 years
25 years
21 years
questions.e: The 1999 Constitution (as amended) fixes the voting age at 18 years. Once a citizen turns 18, he or she can register with INEC and vote.
questions.p: Di 1999 Constitution (wey dem amend) talk say voting age na 18 years. Once citizen reach 18, e fit register with INEC and vote.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of using the secret ballot system during elections?
o: To allow a voter to cast more than one vote
To permit voters to openly declare their choice before everyone
To protect the privacy of a voter's choice from intimidation
To make result collation faster for INEC officials
questions.e: The secret ballot lets a voter mark his choice privately so that no one can intimidate, bribe or victimise him because of how he voted. It protects free choice, not speed or multiple voting.
questions.p: Secret ballot make voter mark im choice for private so nobody go fit threaten, bribe or punish am because of how e vote. Na im dey protect free choice, no be about speed or multiple voting.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an example of political participation by a citizen?
o: Deliberately refusing to pay approved taxes to government
Voting during a general election
Joining and paying dues to a registered political party
Contesting for a seat in the State House of Assembly
questions.e: Political participation involves lawful activities like voting, joining parties and contesting elections that help citizens take part in governance. Refusing to pay tax is tax evasion, an offence, not a form of political participation.
questions.p: Political participation na lawful tin like voting, joining party and contesting election wey make citizen take part for governance. To refuse pay tax na tax evasion, na offence, e no be political participation.

questions.q: During campaign for a local government chairmanship election in Enugu State, Chief Okoro's agents were seen sharing bags of rice and cash of ₦2,000 to voters, promising more money if they thumb-print for him on election day. Which electoral malpractice does this describe?
o: Gerrymandering
Multiple registration
Ballot box snatching
Vote buying
questions.e: Giving voters money or gifts to influence how they vote is called vote buying, a common electoral malpractice. Gerrymandering concerns unfair drawing of constituency boundaries, not cash gifts, so it does not fit here.
questions.p: To give voters money or gift make dem vote one way na vote buying, one common electoral malpractice. Gerrymandering na about how dem dey draw constituency boundary unfair, e no concern cash gift, so e no fit be di answer.

questions.q: In Civic Education, what is meant by "political apathy"?
o: A lack of interest or unwillingness of citizens to take part in political activities
Strict enforcement of electoral laws by INEC
Active involvement of citizens in politics and elections
The formation of new political parties before an election
questions.e: Political apathy means citizens show little or no interest in political matters such as voting, campaigns or joining parties. It is the opposite of active political participation.
questions.p: Political apathy na when people no get interest for politics, like voting or joining party. E dey opposite to when people dey actively take part for politics.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common cause of political apathy among young Nigerians today?
o: Strong enforcement of the electoral laws
Regular conduct of free and fair elections
High level of civic education in schools
Disappointment caused by leaders who fail to fulfil campaign promises
questions.e: When politicians make promises during campaigns but fail to deliver after winning, citizens, especially youths, become discouraged and lose interest in future political activities. This disappointment is a major cause of apathy.
questions.p: When politicians promise plenty things during campaign but no do am after dem win, people go vex and lose interest for politics. Na so this kind disappointment dey cause apathy.

questions.q: What is a major effect of widespread political apathy on a democratic nation?
o: It automatically improves government accountability
It leads to the emergence of leaders who do not truly represent the wishes of the majority
It increases the overall voter turnout during elections
It strengthens the legitimacy of elected leaders
questions.e: When many eligible citizens refuse to vote or participate, a small group decides who leads, so the winners may not truly reflect the wishes of the wider population. This weakens the representative nature of democracy.
questions.p: If plenty people no vote or no participate, na small group go decide who go rule, so the winner no really represent everybody wish. This dey weaken democracy.

questions.q: During election week, Mrs. Chioma, a trader in Onitsha, refuses to go out to vote because she is afraid of being attacked by thugs who usually cause violence at her polling unit. Which cause of political apathy does this situation best illustrate?
o: Strong religious beliefs against voting
Excessive civic education by the government
Fear arising from insecurity and political violence
Widespread illiteracy among voters
questions.e: Mrs. Chioma's refusal to vote is directly linked to fear of violence at the polling unit, which is a case of insecurity discouraging participation. This is different from illiteracy or religion, which are not mentioned in the scenario.
questions.p: Mrs. Chioma no vote because she fear say thugs go attack am for polling unit, na insecurity dey make her stay away. E no be say na illiteracy or religion cause am, na fear of violence.

questions.q: Which of these measures would most effectively help reduce political apathy in a community?
o: Increasing the cost of obtaining a voter's card
Reducing press freedom during election periods
Organising regular civic and voter enlightenment programmes
Delaying the announcement of election results indefinitely
questions.e: Civic and voter enlightenment programmes educate citizens on the importance of participation, which builds interest and confidence in the political process. The other options would discourage participation rather than encourage it.
questions.p: When dem dey teach people civic education and voter awareness, e dey make people understand why dem suppose participate for politics. The other options go instead discourage people from participating.

questions.q: In a certain Local Government Area, only 2 out of every 10 registered voters came out to vote during the council election, because most people said they no longer trusted any of the candidates. What does this situation best show about the effect of political apathy?
o: It improves the quality of electoral administration
It weakens the legitimacy of the officials who eventually get elected
It strengthens grassroots democracy at the local level
It guarantees that the best candidate will always win
questions.e: When only a small fraction (2 out of 10, that is 20%) of voters turn out, the winning candidate is chosen by a very small minority, which reduces the moral authority and legitimacy of the elected official. This shows how apathy can damage democratic representation.
questions.p: If na only 2 out of 10 people (20%) come vote, e mean say small small people choose the winner, so the person wey win no really get strong legitimacy. Na so apathy dey spoil democratic representation.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines constitutional democracy?
o: A system where only one political party is allowed to exist
A system where the military controls government activities
A system where a king makes all laws without any limitation
A system of government in which power is exercised according to the provisions of a written or unwritten constitution
questions.e: Constitutional democracy means government operates under the rules and limits set out in a constitution, which guides how power is used and shared. This prevents any leader or group from ruling without restriction.
questions.p: Constitutional democracy na when government dey rule according to wetin constitution talk, no be anyhow power. The constitution dey guide how dem go use power so nobody go rule anyhow.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT generally regarded as a pillar of democracy?
o: Hereditary monarchy
Free and fair elections
Independent judiciary
Rule of law
questions.e: Hereditary monarchy, where leadership passes automatically through family bloodline, is not a feature of democracy. Democracy is built on rule of law, independent judiciary, and free elections, which allow the people to choose and check their leaders.
questions.p: Hereditary monarchy, wey mean say leadership dey pass from family to family, no be democracy pillar. Democracy dey built on rule of law, independent judiciary and free election wey allow people choose their leader.

questions.q: In the principle of separation of powers under a constitutional democracy, which pairing of an arm of government with its major function is correct?
o: Legislature - interprets the constitution during court cases
Legislature - implements government programmes
Executive - enforces and implements laws made by the legislature
Judiciary - makes laws for the country
questions.e: Under separation of powers, the executive is the arm responsible for enforcing and implementing laws, the legislature makes laws, and the judiciary interprets them. Mixing up these roles would wrongly combine the duties of different arms.
questions.p: Under separation of powers, executive na the arm wey dey enforce and carry out laws, legislature dey make the laws, while judiciary dey interpret am. If you mix the roles, e go wrong.

questions.q: The rule of law, as a pillar of democracy, mainly means that
o: the president can set aside court judgements whenever he wishes
everyone, including government officials, is subject to the law
laws of the land apply strictly during election periods only
only poor citizens are bound to obey the law
questions.e: Rule of law means no one, not even the highest government official, is above the law; everyone is equally subject to it and can be held accountable. This ensures fairness and justice for all citizens.
questions.p: Rule of law mean say nobody dey above the law, even the president or governor. Everybody, big or small, must follow the law and fit face consequence if dem break am.

questions.q: Which Nigerian body is primarily responsible for organising and conducting elections at the federal and state levels, in line with constitutional democracy?
o: Economic and Financial Crimes Commission
Independent Corrupt Practices Commission
National Drug Law Enforcement Agency
Independent National Electoral Commission
questions.e: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is the constitutional body saddled with organising, conducting and supervising elections in Nigeria. The other agencies listed deal with corruption and drug-related matters, not elections.
questions.p: INEC (Independent National Electoral Commission) na the body wey constitution give work to organise and conduct election for Nigeria. The other agencies dey handle corruption and drug matters, no be election.

questions.q: Checks and balances exist in a constitutional democracy so that no single arm of government becomes too powerful. Which of the following scenarios best illustrates this principle in action?
o: The judiciary reviews and declares an act of the National Assembly unconstitutional after examining it
The executive appoints all judges without any legislative screening or approval
The legislature is barred by law from questioning any action of the executive
The legislature passes a budget and the executive implements it without any form of review
questions.e: When the judiciary reviews and can strike down a law passed by the legislature for being unconstitutional, it shows one arm checking the excesses of another, which is the essence of checks and balances. The other options describe situations where one arm has unchecked power, which goes against this principle.
questions.p: When judiciary check law wey legislature pass and reject am because e no follow constitution, na so checks and balances dey work, one arm dey check the other. The other options show one arm wey get power wey nobody fit check, wey no be checks and balances.

questions.q: Mrs. Adeyemi, a civics teacher, tells her class that true constitutional democracy exists only when citizens can freely criticise government policies through newspapers, radio and television without fear of arrest. This statement best relates to which pillar of democracy?
o: Freedom of the press
Judicial precedent
Federal character principle
Fiscal federalism
questions.e: Freedom of the press allows citizens and journalists to express opinions and criticise government actions through the media without being punished. This openness helps keep government accountable, which is central to constitutional democracy.
questions.p: Freedom of the press mean say citizens and journalists fit talk their mind and criticise government through media without dem arrest dem. E dey help make government accountable, and na important part of constitutional democracy.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines 'public service' as used in Civic Education?
o: Private companies licensed to execute government contracts
Trade unions that represent workers across various industries
The totality of government agencies and institutions established to implement policies and deliver services to citizens
All religious organizations that provide charity services to members
questions.e: Public service refers to government ministries, departments and agencies set up to carry out government policies and provide services like health, education and security to the people. The other options describe private or voluntary bodies, not government institutions.
questions.p: Public service na all the government ministries and agencies wey dem set up to carry out government policies and give services like health, education and security to the people. The other options na private or voluntary bodies, no be government ones.

questions.q: A key feature of public service is that civil servants are expected to be politically neutral. This means a civil servant should
o: resign from office anytime a new political party takes over government
campaign openly for the political party he supports
refuse to carry out policies made by an opposition-led government
serve the government of the day loyally regardless of which political party is in power
questions.e: Political neutrality means civil servants are permanent staff who serve whichever government is in power without taking sides. This ensures continuity and stability of government business.
questions.p: Political neutrality mean say civil servant na permanent staff wey go serve whichever government dey power, no matter the party. Dis one dey ensure say government work no go stop or scatter when new party come.

questions.q: A major challenge of public service in Nigeria is bureaucratic bottleneck, often called 'red tape'. This refers to
o: a reduction in the number of official procedures needed
excessive and rigid official procedures that cause unnecessary delay in service delivery
the use of only one signature to approve all files
fast and transparent approval of official documents
questions.e: Red tape describes too many unnecessary official steps and approvals that slow down the delivery of services to the public. It is a common complaint against public service in many countries, including Nigeria.
questions.p: Red tape na when too many unnecessary official steps and approvals dey slow down how government dey give service to people. Na common complain against public service for many country, Nigeria inclusive.

questions.q: Which Nigerian body is specifically responsible for receiving and verifying the asset declaration forms of public officers before and after they leave office?
o: Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC)
Nigeria Police Force
Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
Code of Conduct Bureau (CCB)
questions.e: The Code of Conduct Bureau is the agency set up to receive, keep and verify asset declaration forms of public officers as required by the Constitution. EFCC and ICPC mainly investigate and prosecute corruption, while the Police handle general law enforcement.
questions.p: Code of Conduct Bureau na the agency wey dem set up to collect, keep and check asset declaration forms of public officers as the Constitution talk am. EFCC and ICPC dey more on investigate and prosecute corruption, while Police dey handle general law enforcement.

questions.q: When a public officer gives undue preference to members of his own family or ethnic group in employment or promotion instead of considering merit, this challenge in public service is called
o: accountability
nepotism
meritocracy
transparency
questions.e: Nepotism is the practice of favouring relatives or members of one's ethnic group over more qualified persons when giving jobs or promotions. It weakens efficiency and fairness in public service.
questions.p: Nepotism na when person dey favour im family or im tribe people pass better qualified person for job or promotion. E dey spoil efficiency and fairness for public service.

questions.q: Mrs. Eze, a civil servant in a state Ministry of Education, complains that her monthly salary cannot meet her family needs, so she now collects bribes from contractors before approving their files. This scenario best illustrates which challenge of public service?
o: Poor remuneration leading to corrupt practices
Lack of job security for workers
Over-staffing of ministries
Excessive workload on senior staff
questions.e: Low salaries can push some civil servants into demanding bribes to survive, which is a common cause of corruption in public service. The scenario shows a direct link between poor pay and Mrs. Eze's corrupt behaviour.
questions.p: Low salary fit push some civil servant make dem dey collect bribe just to survive, and na common reason wey dey cause corruption for public service. The story show clear connection between Mrs. Eze poor pay and her corrupt act.

questions.q: Alhaji Sule, a farmer in Kebbi State, waited eight months to collect his fertilizer subsidy voucher because his application had to pass through eleven different offices for approval. Which reform would MOST effectively solve this type of challenge in public service delivery?
o: Transferring the farmer's file to a private company for safe keeping
Increasing the number of offices the file must pass through
Introducing e-governance to simplify and reduce bureaucratic procedures
Employing more junior staff in each of the eleven offices
questions.e: The problem is too many bureaucratic steps causing delay, so the best solution is to simplify processes using e-governance (online applications and tracking), which cuts down unnecessary stages. Adding more staff or more offices would not remove the root cause, which is the long, rigid procedure.
questions.p: The real problem na too many bureaucratic steps wey dey cause delay, so the best solution na to use e-governance (online application and tracking) make the process short well well. To add more staff or more offices no go solve am because the main wahala na the long, stiff procedure.

questions.q: Which government agency is specifically charged with controlling traffic and reducing road accidents on Nigerian highways?
o: Nigeria Immigration Service
Nigeria Customs Service
Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps
Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
questions.e: The FRSC was established to manage traffic, enforce road safety rules, and reduce accidents on Nigerian roads. The other agencies handle immigration matters, border goods, and civil defence respectively.
questions.p: FRSC na the agency wey dem set up to control traffic and reduce accident for Nigerian roads. The other agencies dey handle immigration, goods for border, and civil defence.

questions.q: Amina's younger sister was lured abroad with a fake job offer and forced into labour against her will. Which agency should the family report this case to for investigation and the victim's rescue?
o: National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP)
National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)
Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
Independent Corrupt Practices Commission (ICPC)
questions.e: NAPTIP was specifically set up to prevent human trafficking, protect and rehabilitate victims, and prosecute traffickers. EFCC handles financial crimes, NDLEA handles drugs, and ICPC handles corruption by public officers.
questions.p: NAPTIP na the agency wey dem make to stop human trafficking, help victims, and chase people wey dey traffic persons. EFCC na for money crime, NDLEA na for drug, ICPC na for corruption by government workers.

questions.q: A customs officer at a Nigerian port is found collecting bribes from importers before clearing their goods. Which agency has the primary mandate to investigate this type of corrupt practice by a public officer?
o: Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps
National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)
Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC)
Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
questions.e: The ICPC was created mainly to investigate and prosecute corrupt practices such as bribery and gratification among public officers. The other agencies deal with road safety, drug offences and civil defence, not corruption cases.
questions.p: ICPC na the agency wey get mandate to investigate and prosecute corruption like bribe-taking among government workers. The other agencies dey handle road safety, drug matter and civil defence, no be corruption.

questions.q: Which Nigerian court has original jurisdiction to try serious offences such as murder and treason, which carry the death penalty if proven?
o: Area Court
High Court
Magistrate Court
Customary Court
questions.e: The High Court has unlimited original jurisdiction to try capital offences like murder and treason. Magistrate, Customary and Area Courts have limited powers and cannot try such serious capital cases.
questions.p: High Court get full power to first try serious case like murder and treason wey fit lead to death sentence. Magistrate, Customary and Area Court no get that kind power.

questions.q: Chief Obi, a local government chairman, is accused of diverting public funds meant for community boreholes into his personal bank account. Which agency is primarily empowered to investigate and prosecute this act of corruption by a public office holder?
o: Nigeria Police Force
Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC)
Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps
questions.e: The ICPC's core mandate is to investigate and prosecute corrupt practices, such as diversion of public funds, committed by public officers. Although the police may assist, the specialised body for this specific offence is the ICPC, not the FRSC or Civil Defence Corps.
questions.p: ICPC main work na to investigate and prosecute corruption like when public officer divert government money. Police fit help, but the special agency wey dey handle this kain case na ICPC, no be FRSC or Civil Defence.

questions.q: Malam Bello and his brother are disputing the sharing of their late father's property under Islamic law in Sokoto State. If the case is first decided at the Sharia Court, to which court should an unsatisfied party appeal?
o: Sharia Court of Appeal
Federal High Court
Supreme Court
Customary Court of Appeal
questions.e: Matters decided under Islamic personal law at the Sharia Court are appealed to the Sharia Court of Appeal, which specially handles such cases. The Federal High Court and Customary Court of Appeal deal with different matters, while the Supreme Court is the final appellate court, not the first appeal stage.
questions.p: Any case wey dem decide under Islamic law for Sharia Court, if person no gree, e go appeal go Sharia Court of Appeal wey be the correct court for that kain matter. Federal High Court and Customary Court of Appeal na for different matter, and Supreme Court na final court, no be first appeal.

questions.q: Which government agency is primarily responsible for arresting and prosecuting persons involved in the illegal trafficking of hard drugs in Nigeria?
o: National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP)
Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)
questions.e: The NDLEA is the Nigerian agency specifically set up to fight drug trafficking and abuse. FRSC deals with road safety, NAPTIP with human trafficking, and EFCC with financial crimes.
questions.p: NDLEA na di agency wey dem set up to fight drug trafficking and abuse for Nigeria. FRSC dey handle road safety, NAPTIP na human trafficking, EFCC na financial crime matter.

questions.q: Secret cult groups in Nigerian secondary schools and higher institutions are best described as associations that:
o: Promote academic excellence through mentorship
Use violence and secrecy to achieve selfish aims
Operate openly with government approval
Organise public debates on national issues
questions.e: Cult groups are known for secret initiation, violent activities and selfish or criminal goals. They do not operate with lawful government approval or promote academic welfare.
questions.p: Cult groups na association wey dey hide dia activities and dey use violence to achieve dia own selfish aim. Dem no get government approval and dem no dey promote academic progress.

questions.q: A major long-term consequence of drug abuse among youths is that it:
o: Strengthens family relationships
Improves concentration during examinations
Leads to mental health disorders and reduced productivity
Guarantees quick admission into tertiary institutions
questions.e: Prolonged drug abuse damages the brain and body, causing mental disorders such as psychosis and reducing a person's ability to work or study effectively. It does not improve exam performance or family ties.
questions.p: If person dey abuse drug for long time, e fit cause mental health problem and reduce how di person dey perform well for work or school. E no dey improve exam result or make family relationship better.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why youth empowerment programmes are encouraged as a way to reduce cultism in Nigerian institutions?
o: They replace the need for school discipline and rules
They allow students to form armed groups for self-defence
They force students to pay high fees before graduation
They provide skills and opportunities that reduce idleness and frustration among youths
questions.e: Youth empowerment gives young people skills, jobs and purpose, reducing the idleness and frustration that often push them toward cult groups. The other options either worsen the problem or are irrelevant to empowerment.
questions.p: Youth empowerment dey give young pipo skill and work wey go reduce idleness and frustration wey dey push dem go cultism. Di oda options no dey help solve di problem, dem fit even worsen am.

questions.q: Okonkwo noticed that his classmate Tunde suddenly started skipping classes, had bloodshot eyes, became aggressive, and stopped associating with his old friends. Based on common warning signs taught in civic education, Tunde most likely is:
o: Suffering from a common cold
Possibly abusing hard drugs
Studying extra hard for examinations
Preparing for a sporting competition
questions.e: Sudden change in behaviour, bloodshot eyes, aggression and withdrawal from old friends are classic warning signs of drug abuse taught in civic education. The other options do not match this combination of symptoms.
questions.p: Di sudden change for behaviour, red eye, aggression and how e comot from im old friends na common sign of drug abuse wey dem teach for civic education. Di oda options no fit match wetin dey happen to Tunde.

questions.q: A community in Oyo State records a rise in school dropout and violent cult clashes among teenagers. Which combination of actions would most effectively address the root causes based on civic education principles?
o: Provide vocational training, counselling services and strict enforcement of anti-cultism laws
Relocate all affected teenagers to another state without support
Ignore the situation since it will resolve itself naturally
Increase the price of school uniforms and ban extracurricular activities
questions.e: Addressing root causes requires giving youths skills and guidance (vocational training and counselling) while also enforcing laws against cultism to deter offenders. The other options either worsen conditions or fail to tackle the underlying problems.
questions.p: To solve di root cause, dem need give di teenagers skill and counselling, and still enforce di law against cultism strongly. Di oda options no dey solve anytin, dem fit even make tins worse.

questions.q: Human trafficking is best defined as:
o: the illegal recruitment, transportation, or harbouring of persons through force, deceit, or coercion for exploitation
the voluntary migration of citizens seeking greener pastures abroad
the legal recruitment of workers for overseas employment with full documentation
a government programme for resettling internally displaced persons
questions.e: Human trafficking involves using force, deceit, or coercion to recruit, move, or exploit people, usually for labour or sexual exploitation. Legal migration or voluntary travel is not trafficking because consent and proper process are present.
questions.p: Human trafficking na when dem use force, lie or trick carry person comot, move am or use am do work wey e no gree for. E different from proper legal travel wia everything follow correct process.

questions.q: Which Nigerian government agency is primarily responsible for investigating and prosecuting human trafficking cases?
o: Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC)
Nigeria Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)
National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP)
Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
questions.e: NAPTIP was specifically established to prevent, investigate, and prosecute human trafficking offences in Nigeria. NDLEA handles drug matters, EFCC handles financial crimes, and ICPC deals with corruption.
questions.p: NAPTIP na the agency wey dem set up well-well to fight human trafficking for Nigeria. NDLEA dey face drugs, EFCC dey face money crimes, ICPC dey face corruption.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major push factor that makes young Nigerians vulnerable to human trafficking?
o: effective community policing
poverty and unemployment in their communities
access to quality free education
strong family support systems
questions.e: Poverty and lack of jobs make young people desperate for better opportunities, so they easily fall for traffickers' false promises of good jobs abroad. The other options describe protective factors that reduce vulnerability, not causes.
questions.p: Poverty and lack of work na the main reason wey dey push young people to follow traffickers wey dey promise better life. The other options na things wey dey protect people, no be wetin dey cause the problem.

questions.q: A major consequence of human trafficking on its victims is:
o: enhanced respect in their home community
improved economic status and wealth
automatic free citizenship in the destination country
psychological trauma and serious health risks
questions.e: Trafficking victims often suffer abuse, forced labour, or sexual exploitation, leading to deep psychological trauma and health problems. They rarely gain wealth, respect, or citizenship; instead they are usually exploited and left worse off.
questions.p: Trafficking victims dey suffer mental wahala and health problems because of the abuse wey dem face. Dem no dey get money, respect or citizenship, instead dem dey suffer pass before.

questions.q: Traffickers most commonly lure their victims by:
o: using open recruitment through government job boards
offering genuine scholarships with verified documents
advertising strictly through accredited travel agencies
making false promises of well-paid jobs abroad
questions.e: Traffickers deceive victims with attractive but fake job offers abroad to gain their trust before exploiting them. Genuine scholarships, government recruitment, and accredited agencies follow proper legal processes and are not trafficking tactics.
questions.p: Traffickers dey use sweet lie of good work for abroad to catch people trust before dem go exploit am. Real scholarship, government job or correct travel agency no be wetin traffickers dey use.

questions.q: Chidinma was promised a job as a hairdresser in a foreign country by an agent who, on arrival, seized her international passport and told her she must work without pay for two years to repay the cost of her travel before she can be free. This situation best illustrates:
o: a normal apprenticeship arrangement
debt bondage, which is a recognised form of human trafficking
a standard international employment contract
a voluntary labour exchange scheme
questions.e: Seizing a victim's passport and forcing unpaid labour to 'repay a debt' is a classic trafficking method called debt bondage. A real apprenticeship or legal contract would involve agreed pay, freedom of movement, and the worker's documents remaining with them.
questions.p: When dem seize person international passport make e work free to pay 'debt', na debt bondage, na one kind trafficking be dat. Proper apprenticeship or contract go get agreed pay and the person go still hold im passport.

questions.q: Which international legal instrument is most directly concerned with defining and combating trafficking in persons?
o: Geneva Convention
African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights
UN Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons
Universal Declaration of Human Rights
questions.e: The UN Protocol (also known as the Palermo Protocol) specifically defines trafficking in persons and sets out measures for its prevention and punishment. The other instruments deal with broader human rights or war-related matters, not trafficking specifically.
questions.p: The UN Protocol (Palermo Protocol) na the one wey specifically explain wetin trafficking be and how to fight am. The other ones dey talk about general human rights or war matters, no be trafficking straight.

questions.q: What is the full meaning of HIV, the virus associated with AIDS?
o: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
Human Immune Virus
Human Infectious Virus
Highly Infectious Virus
questions.e: HIV means Human Immunodeficiency Virus. It attacks the body's immune system, making it weak and unable to fight infections.
questions.p: HIV na Human Immunodeficiency Virus. E dey attack body immune system make e weak so e no fit fight sickness again.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a known way that HIV can be transmitted from one person to another?
o: Mother-to-child transmission during childbirth
Mosquito bites
Sharing of unsterilized needles
Unprotected sexual intercourse with an infected person
questions.e: HIV is not spread through mosquito bites because the virus cannot survive or multiply inside a mosquito. It spreads through blood, sexual fluids and from mother to child.
questions.p: Mosquito no fit carry HIV go another person because the virus no dey survive inside mosquito body. HIV dey spread through blood, sex fluid, and from mama to pikin.

questions.q: Which government agency has the primary responsibility of coordinating Nigeria's national response to HIV/AIDS?
o: National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP)
National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)
questions.e: NACA (National Agency for the Control of AIDS) was set up by government to plan, coordinate and monitor Nigeria's HIV/AIDS prevention and control programmes. The other agencies handle drugs, human trafficking and food/drug regulation respectively.
questions.p: NACA (National Agency for the Control of AIDS) na the agency wey dey coordinate Nigeria HIV/AIDS programmes. The other agencies dey handle drug matter, human trafficking and food/drug control.

questions.q: Mrs. Adeyemi, a pregnant woman, is diagnosed HIV positive. What is the most effective step she can take to reduce the risk of passing the virus to her baby?
o: Avoid breastfeeding immediately without medical advice
Stop attending antenatal clinic to avoid stigma
Take prescribed antiretroviral drugs throughout pregnancy, delivery and as advised after birth
Deliver the baby only through a traditional birth attendant
questions.e: Taking antiretroviral drugs as prescribed by health workers greatly lowers the amount of virus in the mother's body, which reduces the chance of mother-to-child transmission. Avoiding clinics or using untrained attendants increases risk instead.
questions.p: If pregnant woman dey take ARV drugs well-well as doctor talk am, e go reduce the virus for her body and lower the chance say the pikin go catch am. To avoid clinic or use untrained birth attendant go increase the risk instead.

questions.q: In a Civic Education class in Enugu, students learn that a person can carry HIV for many years without showing any sign of sickness, even though the virus is slowly multiplying in the body. What is this stage called?
o: Full-blown AIDS
Window period
Seroconversion
Clinical latency (asymptomatic stage)
questions.e: Clinical latency is the long stage where HIV is present and slowly multiplying but the person shows no obvious symptoms, sometimes lasting many years. The window period is the early stage before antibodies can be detected, while full-blown AIDS is the advanced stage with serious symptoms.
questions.p: Clinical latency na the long stage wey person get HIV but e no show any sign, even though the virus dey slowly multiply inside body, e fit reach many years. Window period na early stage before antibody go show, full-blown AIDS na when serious signs don show.

questions.q: Which of the following everyday practices will NOT put a person at risk of contracting HIV?
o: Shaking hands with a person living with HIV
Sharing razor blades with friends
Having unprotected sex with an infected partner
Using unsterilized tattoo or piercing needles
questions.e: HIV is not spread by casual contact like shaking hands, hugging or sharing food because the virus needs direct contact with blood or certain body fluids to spread. Sharing blades, needles and unprotected sex all involve such risky contact.
questions.p: Shaking hand no fit give person HIV because the virus need direct contact with blood or certain body fluid to spread. To share blade, needle or do unprotected sex na risky one because dem fit expose person to blood or fluid.

questions.q: During a school health talk, a resource person stresses that early detection of HIV helps infected persons live longer and helps reduce further spread in the community. Which practice best promotes early detection?
o: Self-medication with herbal concoctions whenever one feels unwell
Depending only on traditional healers for diagnosis
Voluntary Counselling and Testing (VCT) at a health facility
Avoiding health facilities until symptoms become severe
questions.e: Voluntary Counselling and Testing (VCT) allows a person to know their HIV status early through proper laboratory testing, so treatment can start on time and the person can take precautions to protect others. Herbal self-medication and traditional diagnosis cannot accurately detect HIV.
questions.p: Voluntary Counselling and Testing (VCT) na the correct way make person know im HIV status early through proper lab test, so treatment go start on time and e go fit protect other people. Herbal medicine or traditional healer no fit accurately detect HIV.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines interpersonal relationship?
o: A government policy used to control population growth
A law that guides the conduct of marriage ceremonies
The process of registering a new business name
The way people interact and relate with one another in society
questions.e: Interpersonal relationship simply means how people relate, interact and associate with one another, whether at home, school, work or in the community.
questions.p: Interpersonal relationship na how people dey relate and interact with each other, for house, school or work.

questions.q: Responsible parenthood mainly involves parents doing which of the following?
o: Ensuring that their children attend only expensive private schools
Providing adequate care, training and welfare for the children they bring into the world
Giving birth to as many children as biologically possible
Leaving the upbringing of their children permanently to relatives
questions.e: Responsible parenthood means parents deliberately plan for and properly cater for the physical, moral, educational and emotional needs of the children they have, according to their means.
questions.p: Responsible parenthood mean say parents go take care, train and provide for their pikin well-well, according to wetin dem fit afford.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an example of an interpersonal relationship?
o: Working relationship between a boss and an employee
A trade agreement signed between two foreign countries
Friendship between two classmates in a secondary school
Relationship between a mother and her child
questions.e: Interpersonal relationships exist between individuals, such as family, friendship and work relationships. A trade agreement between two countries is an international relationship, not a personal one between individuals.
questions.p: Interpersonal relationship na between persons, like family, friend and work relationship. Trade agreement between two kontri na international matter, e no be personal relationship.

questions.q: One major benefit of family planning to a household is that it helps parents to:
o: Discourage their children from going to school
Increase the number of children beyond what their income can support
Space the birth of their children and manage resources for their proper upbringing
Avoid registering the birth of their children with the government
questions.e: Family planning allows parents to space births and have only the number of children they can comfortably cater for, which improves the children's welfare and reduces financial strain on the family.
questions.p: Family planning dey help parents to space their pikin dem well and take proper care of them, instead of dey born beyond wetin their pocket fit carry.

questions.q: Which Nigerian government agency is primarily responsible for combating human trafficking and protecting children who are exploited as a result of irresponsible parenthood?
o: National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP)
Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
Independent Corrupt Practices Commission (ICPC)
Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
questions.e: NAPTIP was specifically set up to prevent, investigate and prosecute cases of human trafficking, including child trafficking and exploitation that often arise from irresponsible parenting.
questions.p: NAPTIP na the agency wey dem set up to fight human trafficking and protect pikin wey dem dey use for bad bad business because parents no train dem well.

questions.q: Mallam Garba has nine children but earns only ₦20,000 a month as a labourer. Four of his children have dropped out of school and now hawk goods on the street to support the family. This situation best illustrates:
o: Sound economic planning by the family
A strong interpersonal relationship within the family
Effective family planning by Mallam Garba
Irresponsible parenthood on the part of Mallam Garba
questions.e: Having more children than one's income can comfortably support, leading to children dropping out of school to hawk, shows a failure to plan and provide properly for children, which is the opposite of responsible parenthood.
questions.p: Mallam Garba get pikin pass wetin im salary fit carry, so im pikin dem dey hawk for road instead of school. Na clear sign of irresponsible parenthood.

questions.q: Which of the following is a likely long-term effect on a society where many parents fail to practice responsible parenthood?
o: An automatic improvement in the standard of living for all citizens
A reduction in the rate of school dropouts
A steady decrease in the nation's population growth rate
An increase in child labour and juvenile delinquency
questions.e: When parents cannot adequately cater for their children, such children are often pushed into child labour, street begging or crime, which raises the rate of juvenile delinquency in the society over time.
questions.p: If parents no dey take care of their pikin well, plenty of dem go end up dey hustle for street or dey do crime, and dis one go increase child labour and bad behaviour for society.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation FRSC stand for in Nigeria's road transport system?
o: Federal Road Safety Corps
Federal Registration of Safety Commission
Federal Roads and Signals Corps
Federal Road Security Commission
questions.e: FRSC is the Federal Road Safety Corps, the government agency responsible for traffic regulation, road safety education and enforcement of traffic laws in Nigeria.
questions.p: FRSC na Federal Road Safety Corps, na dem be di government agency wey dey control traffic and road safety matter for Nigeria.

questions.q: At a standard traffic light, which colour instructs a driver to come to a complete stop?
o: Amber/Yellow
Red
Green
Blue
questions.e: Red at a traffic light means drivers must stop completely before the stop line until the light changes to green. Amber warns of a change, while green permits movement.
questions.p: Red light for traffic light mean say driver must stop well-well before e go move again. Amber dey warn say light wan change, green na for go.

questions.q: A triangular road sign with a red border and an exclamation mark (!) in the centre is placed along a highway. What does this sign mean to drivers?
o: The road ahead is closed to all vehicles
Overtaking is permitted ahead
There is a general hazard ahead and drivers should be careful
Fuel station is located nearby
questions.e: A triangular sign with a red border and an exclamation mark is a general warning sign; it tells drivers to be cautious because a hazard may be ahead, unlike signs showing a fuel station or road closure.
questions.p: Triangle sign wey get red border and "!" mark na general warning sign; e dey tell driver make dem careful because danger fit dey ahead, e no be fuel station or road closure sign.

questions.q: When a traffic warden stops a motorist on a Nigerian highway for a routine check, which document is the driver legally required to present to show he is permitted to drive?
o: National identity card
Valid driver's licence
Local government indigene certificate
Voter's registration card
questions.e: A valid driver's licence is the legal document that proves a person is trained and permitted to drive; it is what traffic officers check, unlike a voter's card or indigene certificate which have nothing to do with driving.
questions.p: Valid driver licence na legal paper wey show say person fit drive well; na im traffic police go ask for, but voter card or indigene certificate no concern driving.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common and well-known cause of road traffic accidents on Nigerian roads?
o: Regular servicing of vehicle brakes
Strict obedience to posted speed limits
Consistent use of seat belts by passengers
Overloading of vehicles beyond their carrying capacity
questions.e: Overloading a vehicle beyond its capacity makes it hard to control, strains the tyres and brakes, and is a frequent cause of accidents, while the other options actually promote safety.
questions.p: When vehicle carry load pass wetin e suppose carry, e go hard make driver control am well and e go strain tyre and brake; na one common reason wey dey cause accident, di other options na safety things.

questions.q: A driver is moving at a high speed on a rain-soaked road when a child suddenly runs onto the road 20 metres ahead. Why is this driver more likely to hit the child than a driver moving slowly in the same situation?
o: Higher speed reduces the distance needed to stop
The driver's reaction time improves greatly at higher speed
Higher speed increases the stopping distance needed, making it harder to stop in time
Wet roads increase tyre grip at high speed, making stopping easier
questions.e: At higher speed a vehicle needs a longer distance to stop, and a wet road reduces tyre grip even further, so the driver cannot stop quickly enough to avoid hitting the child.
questions.p: If vehicle dey waka fast, e go need more distance before e go fit stop, and if road dey wet, tyre no go grip road well; so driver no fit stop on time to avoid di pikin.

questions.q: At an uncontrolled T-junction without traffic lights or signs, a car on a minor road wants to join a major road just as another car is approaching on the major road. According to standard road safety practice, what should the driver on the minor road do?
o: Give way to the vehicle already on the major road
Insist on entering first because his vehicle is bigger
Enter first since he arrived at the junction earlier
Continue driving since the major road vehicle should give way
questions.e: Standard road safety practice requires a vehicle joining a major road from a minor road to give way to traffic already moving on the major road, in order to prevent collisions at uncontrolled junctions.
questions.p: Normal road safety rule na say vehicle wey dey enter major road from minor road must give way to di one wey dey already for major road, so dat accident no go happen for junction wey no get traffic light.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines 'civil society' as used in Civic Education?
o: A group of citizens who voluntarily organize to pursue shared interests, independent of government control
A political party that contests elections to form government
The armed forces that defend the country from external attack
A government agency that collects taxes and fines from citizens
questions.e: Civil society refers to voluntary associations formed by citizens, separate from government, to pursue common interests such as human rights, welfare or development. It is not a government body, the military, or a political party.
questions.p: Civil society na when citizens come together by themselves, no be government, to chase common interest. E no be government agency, army or political party.

questions.q: Which of these organisations is commonly classified as a civil society organisation in Nigeria?
o: Independent National Electoral Commission
Nigeria Police Force
Federal Ministry of Justice
Nigeria Labour Congress
questions.e: The Nigeria Labour Congress is a voluntary association of workers that is not part of government, making it a civil society organisation. INEC, the Police, and the Ministry of Justice are government bodies.
questions.p: Nigeria Labour Congress na workers association wey no be part of government, so e be civil society. INEC, Police and Ministry of Justice na government bodies.

questions.q: One major feature that distinguishes civil society organisations from political parties is that civil society organisations...
o: are directly controlled by the ruling government
do not seek to win political power or form government
are funded solely by the federal government
must register with INEC as political parties
