questions.e: Civil society groups advocate for causes and influence policy but do not contest elections to control government, unlike political parties. This is their key distinguishing feature.
questions.p: Civil society groups dey advocate for cause but dem no dey contest election to rule. Na wetin different dem from political party wey dey struggle for power.

questions.q: Popular participation in governance is best demonstrated when citizens...
o: refuse to pay any form of tax to government
avoid getting involved in any public issue at all
vote during elections and contribute opinions at town hall meetings
wait silently for government officials to solve community problems alone
questions.e: Popular participation means citizens actively taking part in governance through actions like voting and attending community meetings to express views. Avoiding involvement or refusing civic duties is the opposite of participation.
questions.p: Popular participation mean say citizens dey actively show face for governance, like to vote and talk their mind for town hall meeting. To dey avoid everything no be participation.

questions.q: What is a major importance of civil society organisations to a democratic government?
o: They appoint judges to the Supreme Court
They check government excesses and promote accountability
They are responsible for printing the national currency
They take over the duties of the three arms of government
questions.e: Civil society organisations watch over government actions, expose corruption, and demand accountability, strengthening democracy. They do not perform official government functions like printing money or appointing judges.
questions.p: Civil society dey watch government, expose corruption and push for accountability. Dem no dey print money or appoint judges, na government work be that.

questions.q: In Ogbomoso town, a group of market women formed an association to press the local government to repair a bad road. They gathered signatures, organised peaceful protests, and met council officials, but did not contest for any political office. This association is best described as:
o: a pressure group within civil society
an arm of the local government
a security outfit
a political party
questions.e: The market women's association used peaceful advocacy methods to influence government decisions without seeking political office, which is the exact definition of a pressure group within civil society. It is not a political party, government arm, or security outfit.
questions.p: Di market women use peaceful protest and meeting to push government, but dem no wan rule. Na so pressure group for civil society dey work, e no be political party or government arm.

questions.q: Which of the following situations would most likely discourage effective popular participation in governance?
o: The existence of independent civil society organisations
Availability of several registered political parties
Regular free and fair elections
Widespread illiteracy and low civic awareness among citizens
questions.e: When citizens lack education and civic awareness, they cannot understand their rights or effectively engage in governance, which weakens popular participation. Free elections, civil society groups, and multiple parties actually encourage participation.
questions.p: If people no sabi read or no get civic awareness, dem no fit sabi dia rights or join governance well. Free election, civil society and plenty parties na things wey dey help participation, no be wahala.

questions.q: In the Nigerian national flag, which consists of two vertical green stripes with a white stripe in between, what does the green colour symbolise?
o: The mineral resources found in Nigeria
The unity of the three regions of Nigeria
The agricultural wealth and fertile land of Nigeria
The peace and honesty of Nigerians
questions.e: The green colour on the Nigerian flag stands for the country's rich agricultural land and natural wealth. The white stripe in the middle represents peace and unity.
questions.p: Di green colour for Nigeria flag na im show say Nigeria get rich farmland and natural wealth. Di white for middle na im dey show peace and unity.

questions.q: Which Nigerian student designed the national flag that was officially adopted in 1960?
o: Herbert Macaulay
Nnamdi Azikiwe
Obafemi Awolowo
Taiwo Akinkunmi
questions.e: Taiwo Akinkunmi, a Nigerian student studying in London, designed the national flag which won a national competition before independence in 1960. The other three were prominent nationalist leaders, not the flag's designer.
questions.p: Na Taiwo Akinkunmi, one Nigerian student wey dey study for London, design di flag wey win competition before independence for 1960. Di oda three na big nationalist leaders, dem no design di flag.

questions.q: On the Nigerian coat of arms, the black shield is divided by a silver wavy band representing River Niger and River Benue. What does the black colour of the shield represent?
o: The strength of the nation
The fertile black soil of Nigeria
The unity of over 250 ethnic groups
The wealth from crude oil
questions.e: On the coat of arms, the black shield represents Nigeria's rich, fertile soil which supports agriculture. The eagle above the shield represents strength, while the horses on both sides represent dignity.
questions.p: Di black shield for di coat of arms na im dey show di rich, fertile soil wey Nigeria get wey good for farming. Di eagle wey dey on top na im dey show strength, while di horses na dignity.

questions.q: Which federal agency has the primary responsibility of controlling the cultivation, processing, sale and trafficking of hard drugs in Nigeria?
o: National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)
Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP)
questions.e: The NDLEA was established specifically to enforce laws against the cultivation, processing, sale, trafficking and use of hard drugs in Nigeria. FRSC handles road safety, NAPTIP deals with human trafficking, and EFCC handles financial crimes.
questions.p: NDLEA na di agency wey dem set up to fight against planting, processing, selling and trafficking of hard drugs for Nigeria. FRSC na road safety, NAPTIP na human trafficking, EFCC na financial crime.

questions.q: A 15-year-old girl, Blessing, is rescued after being forced to work without pay in another state by a woman who promised her a better life. Which federal agency is saddled with investigating and prosecuting this type of case?
o: Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP)
Independent Corrupt Practices Commission (ICPC)
questions.e: NAPTIP was created to combat human trafficking and forced labour, especially cases involving women and children like Blessing's. EFCC deals with financial crimes, ICPC with corruption, and FRSC with road matters.
questions.p: NAPTIP na im dem set up to fight human trafficking and forced labour, especially wen e concern woman and pikin like Blessing. EFCC na financial crime, ICPC na corruption, FRSC na road matter.

questions.q: Mr. Eze, a federal civil servant, is caught collecting ₦2 million from a contractor in exchange for approving a government contract without due process. Which federal institution has primary responsibility for investigating this kind of corrupt practice by a public officer?
o: Federal Character Commission
Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
Independent Corrupt Practices Commission (ICPC)
National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA)
questions.e: The ICPC was specifically established to investigate and prosecute corrupt practices committed by public officers in the course of their official duties, such as bribery for contracts. The EFCC mainly handles broader economic and financial crimes like money laundering and fraud across both public and private sectors.
questions.p: ICPC na di one wey dem set up to investigate and prosecute corrupt practice wey public officer do for dia work, like dis bribe for contract matter. EFCC na im dey handle bigger economic and financial crime like money laundering and fraud for public and private sector.

questions.q: The Federal Government wants to ensure that appointments into a newly created federal parastatal reflect the diverse ethnic and state composition of Nigeria, so that no single group dominates. Which federal institution is constitutionally charged with overseeing this arrangement?
o: Federal Character Commission
National Population Commission
Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)
Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission
questions.e: The Federal Character Commission is specifically established to ensure fair representation of Nigeria's diverse states and ethnic groups in federal appointments and institutions. INEC handles elections, the Population Commission handles census, and the Fiscal Commission handles revenue sharing formulas.
questions.p: Federal Character Commission na im dem set up to make sure say different state and ethnic group dey well represent for federal appointment. INEC na election matter, Population Commission na census, Fiscal Commission na revenue sharing.
